text.tspan: I keep a short thread on this. Career growth
is less mysterious than people make it sound.
A mentor asked me what problem I want to be
known for solving.
My note back to the group was basically this.
Relationships compound when you follow
through.
Filing this under things I want to remember.
Your reputation is the sum of closed loops.
I ask for feedback while the project is still
warm, not at review season.
A small public portfolio beats a perfect
private draft.
I renegotiated a recurring task that was
eating my deep-work mornings.
Titles are lagging indicators. Skills are
leading ones.
Ask what success looks like before you start
the work.
Your reputation is the sum of closed loops.
I schedule one skill block a week and defend
it like a client call.
Relationships compound when you follow
through.
Saying no to low-leverage work created space
for visible work.
Titles are lagging indicators. Skills are
leading ones.
I ask for feedback while the project is still
warm, not at review season.
Growth requires recovery time, not just
ambition.
I stopped waiting to be discovered and started
proposing scoped experiments.
Relationships compound when you follow
through.
Saying no to low-leverage work created space
for visible work.
Protect deep work like it is a meeting with
your future paycheck.
